headline: Schwarber, Harper power Phillies past Mariners, 6-0
recap: The Phillies closed out their series in Seattle with a 6-0 win over the Mariners on Wednesday, breaking the game open in the first two innings. Bryce Harper's two-run home run, following a Kyle Schwarber double, staked Philadelphia to a first-inning lead. In the second, Justin Crawford's RBI single scored Bryson Stott, and Kyle Schwarber followed with a three-run homer that scored Brandon Marsh and Crawford, capping a four-run inning. Schwarber's blast was his 40th home run of the season; Harper's was his 27th. Bryson Stott finished with three hits, and Jesus Luzardo was dominant on the mound, striking out nine over seven scoreless innings to improve to 12-5. Jhoan Duran and Tim Mayza each worked a scoreless inning in relief to close it out. Bryan Woo took the loss for Seattle, charged with six earned runs over four innings.

The win snapped a two-game skid and pushed Philadelphia to 74-60, holding second place in the NL East, 4.5 games behind the first-place Atlanta Braves. The Phillies also hold the second NL Wild Card spot, 2.0 games clear of the cutoff.

The Phillies are off Thursday before opening a three-game series at the Angels on Friday. Andrew Painter is set to face Los Angeles right-hander Reid Detmers, with first pitch at Angel Stadium scheduled for 9:38 PM ET.
